The Joint Chiefs of Staff said no violation of South Korean territorial airspace occurred.An air defence identification zone extends beyond national airspace and is used to identify approaching aircraft. Entering it does not by itself mean crossing into a country’s territorial airspace.“Airspace intrusion was anticipated, therefore in order to protect the safety of our people, we issued a warning preemptively,” Jang Do-young, a spokesperson for the Joint Chiefs of Staff, told a briefing on Tuesday.The interior ministry issued the shelter warning at around 7:52 am local time (11:52 pm CET Monday), telling residents to move underground or inside buildings.
